old: [Interpreted] Partial mitigation, reported in fairness. Both zone pairs that do share a study reproduce the direction of the overall polyclonality difference; within 1083-PF-GH-CONWAY, Guinea savanna is more polyclonal than the transitional zone (0.532 versus 0.500 - that is 25 of 47 against 25 of 50, computed on the 4,905 release-QC-pass isolates, since on the 1,900-isolate analysis set the polyclonal fraction is identically zero by construction), matching the overall ordering. That margin is three isolates wide in the denominator, the numerator being 25 in both arms, and should not be read as more than a direction. The zone ordering of polyclonality is therefore reproduced within the one zone pair that shares a study, which is a descriptive check and not a test of cause: holding zone constant still leaves collection year, finer geography, recruitment and host biology varying alongside study. The ordering is not separable from batch for the pairs that carry the largest differences.

old: [Observed] Those conditions occur in this panel, and on the genotypes retrieved for them they change nothing in it; the retrieval scripts and their captured output are archived under provenance_final/audit_scripts and provenance_final/audit_logs. Of the 125 variant records sitting exactly at the 171 panel positions, 16 carry at least one length-changing ALT and 2 have a multi-base REF; a further 19 records anchored outside the panel have a REF span covering a panel position. Genotypes were retrieved for all 32 affected records across all 1,900 isolates. Three have any homozygous non-reference carrier: pfcrt codon 76 with 133, pfcrt codon 271 with 138, and pfdhps codon 431 with 26. In every case the carriers sit on a supported, equal-length allele — codon 76 on ALT1 C, with none on the 55-base insertion; codon 271 on ALT1 GAACGTAAGA, with none on ALT2, none on the spanning deletion and none on the single-base C; codon 431 on ALT1 G, with none on the spanning deletion and none on the 20-base insertion. No isolate anywhere in the panel carries a length-changing allele as a homozygous call, and the 62 mixed calls at these records are removed by the mixed-call rule regardless. The counts reconcile exactly with the reported table: Lys76Thr 133, Gln271Glu 138, Ile431Val 26, and homozygous-reference counts of 1,741 and 1,735 against reported reference-residue counts of 1,741 and 1,735. No residue anywhere in the panel is X, which is consistent with no spanning-deletion allele having been substituted — though that is the panel’s own output checked against itself, not an independent confirmation. The two multi-base REF records differ from the reference at their first base only, so applying one base loses nothing here. And none of the 57 codons is record-free. That is weaker than it sounds, and the weaker form is the accurate one: 46 of the 171 panel positions carry no variant record at all, so at those positions the reference base is read for every isolate whether or not that isolate was covered there. Per codon, 21 have a record at all three positions, 26 at two and 10 at only one, which means the called mask for those 10 rests on a single position’s genotype. Reading absence of a record as the reference allele is therefore an assumption about callability, not a measurement of it; no per-isolate depth field is consulted anywhere in the reconstruction. The counts come from provenance_final/audit_scripts/check_coverage.py. The limitation is real and bounds what the implementation may be applied to; on these inputs it moves no published number. What still rests on an assumption is callability: a codon is called when its constituent genotypes are present and unmixed, which is a statement about the genotype array and not an independent measurement of per-isolate coverage.

new: The BayPass pseudo-observed set is still not MAF-matched; pi.maf truncates only the simulated ancestral frequency (Section 5.6). On the superseded 3,359-SNP calibration the reported threshold was the conservative one, but that experiment does not establish the direction of the error for the final 3,916-SNP run, whose raw pseudo-observed inputs are not archived. The frequency-matching limitation stands; a guaranteed conservative threshold does not. The methods claim had to be withdrawn rather than reproduced.

old: [Interpreted] Two cautions limit how much any of this can be made to mean. First, the fitted quantity is six off-diagonal between-population covariances, and an unrooted four-taxon tree already uses five branch-length parameters, so m = 0 has one residual degree of freedom and m = 1 has none or fewer. A rise in variance explained from 0.897 to 0.941 between those two models is not by itself evidence of gene flow, and the original manuscript's treatment of the m = 0 to m = 1 improvement as "the one substantive result" applied a degrees-of-freedom argument against m = 3 while exempting m = 1 from it. The edge p-values are the stronger evidence precisely because they do not depend on the variance-explained curve. Second, with four populations, three of which are a single administrative region each, these edges cannot be read as specific geographic gene-flow corridors. What the graph establishes is that a strictly bifurcating tree does not describe these populations, which is what would be expected of a single population with ongoing exchange, and that two directions of exchange are statistically supported.

Those are conditional edge statistics, not identified directions of historical exchange.

old: [Interpreted] The containment corollary, correctly scoped. Because no neutral barrier is detectable at the retained common variants, this analysis supplies no evidence of a barrier for a geographically targeted containment intervention to exploit. That is an absence of evidence at the resolution these data permit, not a demonstration that parasite exchange across Ghana is unobstructed: a low differentiation estimate does not measure connectivity, and the study, geography and year confounding is not removed by it. That remains a reasonable reading, and it is now the better supported for the absence of a robust distance effect: there is not even a weak isolation-by-distance gradient left to qualify it. It does not follow that spread will be uniform in rate or that a single site will see it first; the pfaat1, pfdhps and pfdhfr zone differences show that selection and drug pressure impose their own geography on top of free gene flow.
